title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination

monster.name: Nexus Sovereign
monster.title: Counter of Equidistant Trajectories
monster.defeatQuote: Ways to reach node n - 1 with minimum travel time computed modulo 10^9 + 7!

description: You are in a city that consists of `n` intersections numbered from 0 to `n - 1` with bi-directional roads `roads` where `roads[i] = [ui, vi, timei]`. You want to find how many ways there are to travel from intersection 0 to intersection `n - 1` in the shortest amount of time. Return the number of ways modulo `10^9 + 7`.
starterCode:
def countPaths(n: int, roads: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    pass
solutionCode:
def countPaths(n: int, roads: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    import heapq
    from collections import defaultdict
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    for u, v, t in roads:
        graph[u].append((v, t))
        graph[v].append((u, t))
    dist = [float('inf')] * n
    ways = [0] * n
    dist[0] = 0
    ways[0] = 1
    pq = [(0, 0)]
    while pq:
        d, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
        if d > dist[u]: continue
        for v, t in graph[u]:
            if d + t < dist[v]:
                dist[v] = d + t
                ways[v] = ways[u]
                heapq.heappush(pq, (dist[v], v))
            elif d + t == dist[v]:
                ways[v] = (ways[v] + ways[u]) % MOD
    return ways[n - 1]
hints: Dijkstra tracking both minimum distance and number of shortest paths to each vertex.
